interpretation: CPU operator and annotation totals are inclusive; nested events overlap and cannot be added.
CUDA runtime API durations are host elapsed time, including blocking synchronization.
Actual GPU kernel/transfer durations come from kernel/gpu_memcpy/gpu_memset events, not GPU annotations.
Kernel duration sums may overlap across streams; per-device interval unions avoid double counting.
GPU annotation spans include launch gaps and overlap; they are not kernel busy time.
Selected-operator attribution uses External id or a CUDA runtime correlation join; it does not infer causal waiting solely from temporal overlap.
The trace is a separate diagnostic, not an uninstrumented timing sample.
This existing profile motivates the position-metadata candidate; it does not measure the candidate's saved time.
Scalar-read attribution does not independently identify every call as a KV-position read; code inspection supplies that mechanism.
No full trace is read or rehashed by this evidence summarizer.

gpu_ownership.prefix_scope: Hash covers exactly the first source_csv_prefix_bytes bytes, ending on a complete CSV line. The monitor continues and later bytes are not part of this receipt.
gpu_ownership.timestamp_basis: Local timestamps as emitted by nvidia-smi and benchmark logger; timezone not encoded in these files.
gpu_ownership.window_basis: Optimizer setup log through final median report, inclusive of warmup and every measured step. Final timestamp extended by one second for second-resolution logger.

excluded_attempts.status: CUDA OutOfMemoryError during checkpoint loading; no benchmark timing samples used.
excluded_attempts.reason: Failed attempt precedes the cycle2 GPU ownership CSV prefix.

limitations: Polling is approximately 1Hz; subsecond competing processes cannot be ruled out.
Compute-process inventory does not establish absence of graphics work or CPU contention.
Monitor continues; prefix digest is intentionally not a whole-file digest.
Only the four successful warmup and measured windows are audited; checkpoint loading, the earlier failed attempt, and later profile/test windows are excluded.
Additional PID samples during the short-reference cold step are retained explicitly. Their effect on cold-step timing or later device state is not established.
A listed additional compute PID indicates a separate CUDA process; CSV does not establish its ancestry, owner, or actual GPU utilization.
gpu_ownership.sample_count_definition: Legacy sample_count counts per-process CSV rows; poll_count counts distinct polling timestamps. Multiple PIDs at one poll produce multiple process rows.
gpu_ownership.measured_window_basis: Starts at the last warmup step completion log (rounded down to seconds), ends one second after final median log. This conservatively includes the measured region plus up to one second around its boundaries; there are no wall-clock start timestamps inside results.json.
gpu_ownership.warmup_observation: Short reference retry observed additional PID 3299255 using 450-452 MiB at four polls from 14:53:30.004 to 14:53:33.007, before warmup step 0 completed at 14:53:58. All audited measured windows have only the benchmark PID. Process ancestry and ownership are absent from the CSV, so this PID is not proven unrelated.

interpretation: These are separate instrumented step-4 diagnostics, excluded from the primary paired timing samples.
No performance gain is inferred from instrumented profile durations; the matched uninstrumented pairs supply timing evidence.
Scalar operator counts remain equal, while correlated scalar D2H copies and host synchronizations decrease by 4436.
Moving position metadata to CPU is consistent with this mechanism; correlation alone does not classify every scalar call by source line.
CPU operators and annotations have inclusive nested durations; do not sum them or add them to GPU durations.
CUDA runtime durations are host elapsed times. Actual kernel and transfer durations are device events; interval unions avoid stream overlap, subject to timestamp floating-point rounding.
Equal workload and scalar receipt fields are checked here; full tensor parity is established separately by the paired-run reports.
Ownership monitoring coverage reported elsewhere concerns benchmark windows, not these diagnostic profiles.

runs.name: cycle2-depth2-three-updates
runs.selector_provenance: Execution selection supplied by the parent agent and matching retained fixture name; quiet pytest log itself does not print node IDs.
scope: Single CUDA device, deterministic SDPA, depth-2 residual feature head with all six head parameters trainable.
Three generated updates per arm compare compiler reset on every step against retained compilation on the same candidate source.
Scripted token choices and mixed binary fixture rewards preserve native token logits, stochastic feature decisions, packed encoder, cross-attention, backward, and fused MuonAdamW.
Each update requires nonzero gradients and parameter changes for every trainable head parameter; frozen parameters, absent frozen gradients, and optimizer exclusion are checked.
Zero-tolerance equality covers prompt tensors, trajectories, advantages, replay metrics, token logits, head gradients, updated head parameters, and optimizer state.
limitations: The fixture scripts token choices and reward outcomes; it is neither native-task accuracy evidence nor a performance benchmark.
This test compares compiler modes on the candidate source; CPU-position versus CUDA-position numerical comparison is covered by separate cache tests and paired real-model receipts.

runs.name: cycle2-depth2-restart
runs.selector_provenance: Execution selection supplied by the parent agent and matching retained fixture name; quiet pytest log itself does not print node IDs.
scope: Real-tokenizer CLI, one CUDA rank, deterministic SDPA, train_feature_head_only=True, depth-2 head, ARC-Easy/ARC-Challenge/MMLU/GSM8K.
Three optimizer updates save complete checkpoints after each step and exercise process re-execution.
Forked resume from step 1 exactly matches final model tensors, optimizer parameters/state, and serialized rank RNG; saving only at step 3 verifies uninterrupted model and optimizer equivalence.
The complete six-parameter head manifest, optimizer membership, frozen trunk/LM head, and persisted head depth/task identity are checked.
A separate evaluation CLI checks one validation example for each canonical task.
limitations: The test does not explicitly require nonzero native reward or nonzero gradients.
This is a tiny correctness fixture, not 3B restart performance evidence or multi-GPU/Hopper qualification.

final_source_cuda_qualification.timing_interpretation: Pytest wall times include fixture setup and validation and are not optimizer-step performance measurements.
final_source_cuda_qualification.qualification_scope: Two additional final-source single-GPU correctness checks; independent CPU/cache tests are described in the human report.
